newsitem.title: UK: UK Oftel may give Mercury more price freedom.
newsitem.headline: UK Oftel may give Mercury more price freedom.

text.p: British telecommunications watchdog Oftel said on Friday it proposed allowing Mercury more freedom so that it no longer needs to publish specific prices in the market where it is not well established.
Mercury is part of Cable and Wireless Communications -- Britain's biggest telephone and cable television group.

Oftel director-general Don Cruickshank said under his proposals, Mercury would no longer be a well establised operator in the market for retail international services to the U.S., Canada and Germany -- or for international services to other operators on the U.S. route.

However, he said Mercury would have to publish prices for international services to other operators on the Canadian and German routes as well as in all other markets for international services to other operators and for international retail services.
Well established operators have to publish their tariffs and cannot discriminate between customers.
Oftel added that it was also unlikely to regard any "preference of discrimination" that Mercury exercised in those markets as overdue.
Conditions to deal with any anti-competitive behaviour will remain in Mercury's licence.

"Our aim is to avoid over-regulation of Mercury but to have sufficient safeguards in place to ensure that it cannot act anti-competitively both in markets in which it had market power and in adjacent markets where it can use that power," he said.
Until December 1996, only Mercury and British Telecommunications Plc were licensed to provide international facilities. There are now 50 international operators.
